newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Trinidad trawler skipper shot, Venezuela accused.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad trawler skipper shot, Venezuela accused.

text.p: A Trinidadian trawler captain was shot and wounded off the island's south coast on Wednesday and fishermen accused a Venezuelan navy vessel of carrying out the attack.
Trinidad's Foreign Affairs Ministry said it had launched a an investigation into the shooting, which it called "extremely unfortunate".

The victim, Ralph Lewis, was picked up bleeding from his drifting fishing trawler in the Gulf of Paria and airlifted to the San Fernando Hospital in South Trinidad, a ministry statement said. He was in a stable condition.

The president of the Trinidad Trawler Owners Association, Bruno Marharaj, told a local television station that Lewis was shot by a Venezuelan navy boat as he was operating in Trinidadian territorial waters in the Columbus Channel.
Another local fisherman was killed in a similar incident two weeks ago.

Foreign Minister Ralph Maraj said in the statement that Wednesday's shooting took place at a time when Trinidad and Venezuela were discussing matters dealing with security and co-operation in patrolling the gulf.
"Whatever steps need to be taken will be done to uncover what really happened," he said.
The gulf, which separates Trinidad and Venezuela, has been a source of conflict between fishermen from both countries for years.
